_doc: Acknowledged reds — vibe-ic#1025. Adjudicated by
vibe-ic-marketplace/plugins/vibe-ic/programs/gate_red_since_check.py.
A row here grants NO leniency. The hygiene suite still exits 1 for every
FAIL exactly as it did before this file existed, so there is nothing a row
can silence and no green a row can buy. The ONLY thing a row does is start
a clock that gate_red_since_check will fail on once `max_commits` is
exceeded. Adding a row is therefore taking on a deadline, never escaping
one.
Delete the row in the SAME commit that fixes the gate. A row that outlives
its truth is failed as `stale`, because a stale acknowledgement is
indistinguishable to the next reader from a live one, and it is the row
that gets believed.
FIELDS
gate         the gate's label EXACTLY as tools/ci/_gate_dispatch.sh
records it. A label that matches nothing in the record is
failed as `stale`, so a drifting label cannot go quiet.
since        the commit at which the gate went red. The clock is commits
and not wall time so that every reader of the same tree
computes the same age with no persisted run history.
max_commits  how many commits this red may survive before this file
fails the landing gate. Required — an acknowledgement with
no bound never comes due, which is the state being removed.
owner        the issue or PR that will close it.
why          why it is red, in one sentence, for the reader who finds
this file six weeks from now.
NOTE ON CORPUS-DEPENDENT GATES: a gate whose subject left this repository
can be red on one host and green on another with the same commit checked
out. `since` counts commits HERE, so for such a gate a row states a
condition, not a deadline. Read `adjudicated` before believing `since`.
adjudicated  present when a ruling has been written down for this row: the
verdict and where to read it. A row carrying one is NOT to be
renewed by moving `since` forward -- the ruling replaced the
question the deadline was asking.
bound_because why max_commits is THAT number and not a larger one. Not read
by the adjudicator -- read by the reviewer, who is the only
defence against a bound chosen for comfort. A bound whose
reason is 'so the board stays green' is the thing this file
exists to catch.

acknowledged.why: area_total_vs_budget_check and tapeout_docs_gen are AUDIT_ONLY and declare no intent, so nothing invokes them where they could block and nothing says that was the decision.
acknowledged.bound_because: The engineering is one declaration per program; what is slow is the ruling on whether these two block, which is a person's decision and not a build. 70 commits is one day at the measured rate of 72-83 commits/day over 2026-08-19..21. A decision that needs longer than a day is a decision nobody is making.

acknowledged.why: floorplan_hints, power_budget_uw and sdc_constraints_path are read by a checker and populated in 0 of the 4 documents that carry them, so the consumer cannot tell empty from clean.
acknowledged.bound_because: The fix is in vibeic/benchmark-data, not in this repo: either the L-docs populate the three fields or the checker declares them optional, and a cross-repository change needs a round trip. 210 commits is three days at the measured rate. It is the longest bound here and it is still 290 short of the ceiling.
acknowledged.adjudicated: REAL FINDING where the published corpus is REACHABLE, and rc 0 PASS where it is not — MEASURED both ways 2026-08-22. `c5d7f2d00` moved the corpus out of this repo, and this gate resolves it by walking the PROGRAM's parent directories, so its verdict now depends on what sits above the checkout rather than on this repo's history alone. The `since` below is therefore true FOR A HOST THAT CAN REACH A CORPUS and is not a commit-dated deadline in the sense the other rows carry. NOT renewed, and not to be read as blocking a corpus-less landing host. docs/research/2026-08-21-corpus-gate-adjudication.md

acknowledged.why: 113 baseline entries now resolve and must be shrunk out of the baseline before it becomes a standing waiver, and 4 documents cite proofs they do not ship.
acknowledged.bound_because: Two halves with different costs: shrinking the baseline is one --write-baseline run, and the 4 dangling citations need someone to decide whether the document or the missing file is wrong. 140 commits is two days at the measured rate, which is the decision half; the mechanical half could be done today.

acknowledged.why: closed_loop_edge_check, ppa_pr_scope_check and slot_pad_budget_check are run by nothing but their own tests, so a fixture the author wrote proves the logic and never the artefacts.
acknowledged.bound_because: Wiring three checkers into a real runner is a known, cheap edit -- pre_commit_check.sh is the established home for exactly this. 70 commits is one day at the measured rate. This bound is deliberately not padded for the fact that the same three programs also redden the next row: one cause does not earn two graces.

acknowledged.why: the same three programs -- closed_loop_edge_check, ppa_pr_scope_check, slot_pad_budget_check -- are consulted by no automatic verdict, so the tree looks identical whether they would pass or fail.
acknowledged.bound_because: Same cause and same fix as the row above, so the same one-day bound. Two rows rather than one because the gate labels are two and a row whose label matches nothing is failed as stale.

acknowledged.why: 5 declaration regexes scan text no stripper touched, across crosslayer_rewrite_equivalence, declared_clock_period and slot_pad_budget_check, so a comment sentence can mint a module that does not exist.
acknowledged.bound_because: Five call sites, each a one-line change to strip the value that reaches the scan rather than a sibling. 70 commits is one day at the measured rate, and this is generous for five one-line edits -- the bound is set by review, not by typing.

acknowledged.why: step 31 declares reports/phase3/drc_signoff.json and the d3 evidence manifest has never measured it, so the flow and fixtures/matrix_d3_output_manifest.json are out of step.
acknowledged.bound_because: MEASURED, not estimated: this gate went red at origin/main~85 and was green again by origin/main~25, so the previous instance of this exact defect was repaired in under 60 commits by the people who repair it. The bound is that observed repair time, which is the only number here that is a measurement of the fix rather than a judgement about it.

acknowledged.why: the shrink-detector literal in test_liar_census.py lags the flow's declared clause count again -- the fourth time (169->170, 170->175, 175->178, and now).
acknowledged.bound_because: MEASURED from the three previous instances: the literal was repaired in 2 commits between origin/main~249 and ~247, and in under 15 commits between origin/main~85 and ~70. 35 commits is half a day and more than twice the worst observed repair. The bound intentionally does NOT cover the structural fix the test's own docstring asks for -- deriving the floor from the flow -- because what closes this red is the bump, and pricing the bound at the structural fix would be buying four days of silence for a five-minute edit.
